verifiedFindings: Only 1 of 7 CRM vendors (Zoho CRM) includes sales sequences/cadences on its entry paid plan; the other 6 (Pipedrive, Close, HubSpot, Freshsales, Salesforce, monday CRM) require at least one upgrade beyond the cheapest paid tier
5 of 7 include two-way email sync on their entry (or free) plan; Pipedrive and monday CRM require an upgrade first
monday CRM is the only vendor of the 7 with a confirmed minimum seat count to purchase (3 seats)
Annual billing is required to get the advertised entry price at 3 of 7 vendors (Close, HubSpot, Freshsales)
3 of 7 (Pipedrive, Close, monday CRM) disclose no cap on the number of pipelines
audience: Sales leaders and RevOps evaluating a CRM switch
Small-team founders pricing out their first real CRM
assets.pitchAngle: A CRM's advertised price doesn't say which plan you actually need -- this dataset checks the actual feature-gate position (not price) across 7 major CRMs, and it deliberately isn't a ranking.
assets.deepLinkTarget: https://miloosh.com/research/crm-plan-gates-2026 (link the specific finding, e.g. the sequences-gate row, not the homepage)
claimsThatMustNotBeMade: Do NOT present this as a CRM ranking or a 'best CRM' recommendation -- it explicitly is not one, and the page itself states this; a pitch implying otherwise misrepresents the asset
Do NOT claim any of the 7 vendors is 'better' or 'worse' based on gate position -- a gated feature is a packaging fact, not a quality judgment
Do NOT state unknown fields as confirmed (e.g. Salesforce's pipeline cap, Freshsales' plain-SKU contact limits are explicitly unconfirmed -- say so if referenced)
Do NOT call this an 'index' -- it computes no composite score

verifiedFindings: 9 of 16 customer support platforms now confirmed to publish a distinct, separately billed AI-usage price (was incorrectly reported as 5 of 16 before this session's re-verification)
Kayako is the only vendor whose AI-usage price is public while its base seat price is not (contact-sales only) -- the inverse of the usual transparency pattern
Zendesk names a separate AI-usage billing unit ('Automated Resolutions') without publishing its dollar rate -- a third, distinct disclosure pattern

HappyFox, previously entirely unpriced in this research (page unreachable during original research), is now confirmed to have two separately metered AI products (Chatbot $0.33/resolution, Autopilot as low as $0.02/action)

Only Intercom's disclosed AI rate can be turned into a full monthly-cost formula from public information alone -- the other 8 disclosed rates each have a missing input (an undisclosed allowance, an undisclosed seat price, or a variable/tier-dependent rate)
